key_insight: EgoExplorer provides a wearable, in-situ dataset that jointly captures vision, motion, and touch during human loco-manipulation. This gives researchers a more complete view of how locomotion, posture, and object interaction co-evolve in real-world tasks.
problem_solved: Current human demonstration datasets often capture only partial information about loco-manipulation, making it hard to learn coordinated movement and interaction policies. This paper addresses the need for a lightweight, portable system that can collect richer multimodal data across diverse environments.
method: Built a wearable observatory system to record human loco-manipulation in natural settings.
Collected a 100-hour dataset spanning synchronized vision, motion, and touch signals.
Designed the capture setup to support scalable data collection outside controlled lab environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, EgoExplorer enables better imitation learning, humanoid control, and multimodal behavior modeling by providing more realistic demonstration data. It is especially useful for training systems that must understand coordinated movement and physical interaction in the wild.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing the wearable system capturing vision, motion, and touch simultaneously.
A multimodal timeline illustrating how locomotion, posture, and object contact change during a task.
A comparison graphic between prior partial-view datasets and EgoExplorer's full observatory coverage.
Icons for wearable sensors, camera view, motion tracking, and tactile sensing.
paper_title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
paper_authors: Yunsong Zhou, Xuekun Jiang, Haiqi Shen, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi
